parsed.reason: Facts are right: PD Day, tomorrow, all-day, no clock time, no invented consequence, no link. But the phrase "it's an all-day one on the calendar" is calendar talk: it explains how the event is stored or classified instead of telling the parent what is on, so it is unrequested filler and caps the score at 3. It also reads a bit clumsy and notification-like ("an all-day one on the calendar"), not how a friend would text it; a friend would say something like "Tomorrow is a PD day."
